newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts dismayed over Siemens forecast.
newsitem.headline: Analysts dismayed over Siemens forecast.

text.p: Equities analysts expressed dismay on Wednesday at Siemens AG's announcement that it expected no improvement in business results in 1996/97.
"A catastrophe! The major disappointment is the forecast for this year," said analyst Hans Peter Wodniok at Credit Lyonnais in Frankfurt.
"Management has been predicting years of double-digit profit growth but now we see it was just one year. Our confidence in them is gone," he added.
Analyst Peter Roe at Banque Paribas Capital Markets in London agreed. "The share will be friendless for awhile. But confidence may be rebuilt as more information comes out,"
Siemens shares were hammered in heavy after-hours trading on disappointment over the poor outlook.
The stock lost about seven percent to about 73 marks. After outperforming the Frankfurt DAX index in 1995, Siemens shares are now trading below last December's levels.
"The stock price will not have the potential to outperform the market for at least one year, until they have a positive surprise for us. That is more than disappointing," Wodniok said.
While some analysts had forecast 1996/97 earnings at up to 5.80 marks a share, those predictions will now be scaled back to about 4.70 marks, he said.
The company reported that group net profit in 1995/96 was 2.49 billion marks, up from 2.08 billion marks the year before.
A 356 million mark extraordinary profit from the sale of a printer division and 140 million mark gain from an accounting change in currency hedging boosted net profit to 2.99 billion marks.
The 1995/96 results were largely in line with expectations, and some areas were even better than expected, both analysts agreed.
"Semiconductor fears were overdone, and telecommunications have done better then expected," Roe said in explaining the poor 1996 stock performance.

But people now see that Siemens semiconductor business was strong in the first half of this year despite difficulties reported by its rivals, but that that performance is unlikely to be repeated, he said.
"This year will not have the same benefit, and profits will be depressed throughout the year," Roe said.
